column1: # Iannuzzi 2020 NHD Risk Score — predicted probability lookup table
# Source: Iannuzzi JC et al. J Vasc Surg 2020;71:889-95. Table III / Fig 1.
# METHOD (CHANGED 2026-07-26): this is now a MONOTONE (isotonic / PAVA) fit
# pooling both the derivation and validation series below
# earlier raw-derivation-column lookup. The raw derivation column has a
# non-monotonic tail (score 17 = 50%
# artefact (very few patients scored 17 in either cohort) that made the
# highest-risk patients in this score band look lower-risk than mid-range
# patients when used directly as a probability mapping. Peer review flagged
# this as a defect in the published-lookup specification. Pooling both series
# and fitting a single non-decreasing (isotonic) curve via R's stats::isoreg()
# resolves the inversion using all available data rather than discarding
# either series. Weighting is UNWEIGHTED (each series contributes one
# observation per score) because the paper does not report per-score bin
# counts for either series; if those denominators become available
# with counts as isoreg() weights.
# RAW COLUMNS (for provenance — NOT used directly by the pipeline):
#   (validation series has no reported values for scores 17-18; derivation-only there.)
# Fit computed as:
#   pooled_score <- c(0:18
#   pooled_rate  <- c(derivation
#   fit <- isoreg(pooled_score[order(pooled_score)]
#   risk(score) <- fit$yf value for that score (ties share one fitted value by PAVA construction)
# Notable effect: scores 14-17 pool into a single fitted value (0.8249) because
# score 17's low raw rate (0.500) is only reconcilable with 14-16's high raw
# rates (~0.8+) by averaging across that whole block — this is the isotonic
# fit correctly absorbing the score-17 small-sample noise rather than letting
# it invert the curve.
# Low risk (0–4): NHD ~10%  |  Moderate (5–9): ~37%  |  High (≥10): ~66%
# (paper's own SCORE-based strata — see Table 5's Iannuzzi published-strata panel
# which uses these score bands directly rather than this probability mapping)
score
